inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 consolidated cash flow statement add-back 'Stock-based compensation and other stock-based payments (Note 25)' 27.1 (ATD.TO_Annual_FY2026.txt:4902). No separate equity-award withholding tax is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every year); the FY2026 'Share repurchases and associated taxes' line is the Canadian 2% buyback tax, not an equity-award tax, and is not added.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2026 financing-activity outflow 1,572.3 (30m shares). Flat count is FUNDED: the company repurchases far more than SBC issuance (count 1,106.7m FY2021 -> 918.9m Q1 FY2027). Buybacks are value-neutral in this model; the per-share compounding they deliver is not credited beyond the flat count.
inputs.share_count_basis: 918.9m = Q1 FY2027 weighted-average diluted shares (Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:1266). Period-end basic 917.9m (2026-07-19) and 917,962,609 at 2026-08-27 plus 2,546,255 options; treasury-method dilution ~0.6m. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows; no non-SBC issuance is planned (Zabka is debt-funded).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in USD; TSX quote in CAD. USD->CAD 1.4254 (Yahoo CAD=X, 2026-10-10T04:21Z; CADUSD=X 0.7016 inverse 1.4253). Parity check against the US OTC line ANCTF: C$77.65 / 1.4254 = US$54.48 vs observed ANCTF US$54.61 at the same close, a 0.2% tie proving rate, direction and quote basis. Model computes per-share values in USD and converts at this rate; unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are CAD (quote), the _usd twins are the model currency.
inputs.fiscal_year_end: last Sunday of April (FY2026 ended 2026-04-26; 52 weeks)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular TSX close (Friday); not an after-hours print
inputs.net_debt_note: Q1 FY2027 balance sheet (2026-07-19): short-term debt and current LTD 0.7 + long-term debt 10,328.6 = borrowings 10,329.3, less cash 3,198.3 = net debt 7,131.0. The EUR750m (US$876.5m) notes repaid 2026-05-06 are already out of this figure. Lease liabilities (552.3 current + 4,497.6 non-current = 5,049.9) are EXCLUDED under lease treatment (B); the company's own 'net interest-bearing debt' of 12,180.9 is the lease-inclusive figure and the Metrics.csv total_debt series (16,446.0 at FY2026) is likewise lease-inclusive. The pending Zabka purchase (US$8.6bn, debt-funded, expected to close before end-FY2027) is NOT in net debt because its flows are not in the projections either -- see notes.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows. Rf 4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~0.75 (defensive convenience/fuel retailer) -> cost of equity ~8.0%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (FY2026 issues: US$ notes ~5%, CA$ 5.59%), after-tax ~3.9%. Market weights: equity ~US$50bn (918.9m x US$54.5) vs borrowings US$10.3bn ex-lease -> D/V ~17%. WACC = 0.83 x 8.0 + 0.17 x 3.9 = 7.3%, rounded up to 7.5% for the house build. Same WACC in all three scenarios: fuel-margin cyclicality, nicotine decline and Zabka execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. FY2026 lease cash = principal 581.7 (financing; AnnualFinancialStatements_FY2026.txt:820) + interest on lease liabilities 188.8 (AFS:4938) = 770.5 = 1.01% of revenue, charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities (5,049.9 at 2026-07-19) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. D&A for the cash-tax EBIT is ex right-of-use depreciation: FY2026 total D&A and impairment 2,358.4 less ROU depreciation 611.2 (Note 15, AFS:1732) = 1,747.2 = 2.28% of revenue. Short-term and variable lease expense (134.9) is already inside reported EBITDA and is not deducted again.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; non-controlling interests deducted once in the equity bridge at book (128.1 at 2026-07-19, Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:1483). NCI share of earnings is immaterial (6.1 in FY2026 on 3,150 consolidated), so the bridge deduction and the attributable flows differ by rounding.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Company-defined adjusted EBITDA (net earnings + tax + net financial expenses + D&A and impairment, adjusted for acquisition costs and one-off gains): FY2026 6,713.8 = 8.78% of revenue (MD&A FY2026:722). Reported EBITDA 7,023.6 includes the 260.9 interchange-fee legal recovery and the 66.4 GetGo divestiture gain; neither is a base. Share of JV earnings (24.1) sits inside EBITDA per the company definition and is left there (JV distributions roughly match).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2026 interest income 170.0 sits in net financial expenses, below EBITDA, so it is outside the engine's flows by construction. It is not deducted from last_fcf because the company is a net borrower (net debt 7.1bn ex-lease); the 3.2bn cash pile is netted against debt in the bridge instead.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf = reported FCF 3,372.7 (OCF 5,363.2 - capex 1,990.5) - SBC 27.1 - interest income 0 = 3,345.6. Reported OCF is after interest paid (724.5) and before lease principal (581.7); the engine's unlevered, lease-charged FY1 owner FCF lands in the same range because the after-tax interest and the lease principal are of similar size -- a coincidence, not a reconciliation.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner-fcf.md + adaptations a/b/c/f), 10-year explicit horizon FY2027-FY2036, end-of-year discounting, TV = max(0, min(Gordon, cap x FCF_N)). Routed as a non-US operating company: USD filer quoted in CAD, material IFRS-16 leases, small NCI, cyclical fuel margins. REVENUE IS NOT THE GROWTH MEASURE for this business: 73% of revenue is fuel at pass-through prices, so revenue swings with crude (FY2021 45.8bn -> FY2023 71.9bn) while gross profit does not; Q1 FY2027 revenue +25% was largely fuel price. The drivers are therefore chosen so that revenue x margin tracks management's Feb-2026 'Core + More' framework (adjusted EBITDA +6-8% CAGR FY2027-30, merchandise revenue +4-5%, fuel gross profit with inflation, Fit-to-Serve ~$850m cost program by FY2030), with the base at the low end. FUEL MARGIN CYCLE: FY2026 US fuel margin 47.49 cpg vs 45.4/45.3 the two prior years, Europe 11.73 c/l vs 9.50/8.73; Q1 FY2027 US 52.61 cpg vs 44.00. FY2026-27 EBITDA is therefore partly a margin peak; the base lets Y1 ride it (adj EBITDA +6.5%) and the bear mean-reverts it. ZABKA (announced 2026-07-31, PLN 32.6bn / US$8.6bn equity, >13,000 franchise stores Poland+Romania, debt-funded, close expected before end-FY2027, subject to EU/Polish clearance): excluded from the explicit flows AND from net debt, i.e. treated as NPV-neutral at the offer price (~10-11x EBITDA, in line with ATD's own lease-inclusive EV/EBITDA). The bull case carries accretion through higher Y2-Y5 growth and margin; the bear carries integration drag and the leverage it adds (lease-inclusive leverage ~1.8x -> ~2.6x pro forma). Management's guidance explicitly excludes it. SBC is 0.035% of revenue, so the house/street band is a few cents wide -- band_position is not meaningful here and should be read as collapsed. No prior DCF exists for this ticker (fresh build; no reconciliation block).

equity_bridge.note: Quarterly_Q1-2027.txt:1483, balance at 2026-07-19; consolidated flows, charged once here

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment anchored to the equity 5yr CAGR (5.8%, which includes ~3%/yr of buyback shrinkage) and the Core + More merchandise-revenue guide of 4-5%/yr; used as the mid-horizon revenue growth in the base path
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 5yr CAGR 10.8% vs equity 5.8% and owner-FCF 3.1%: the FY2021 base year is the COVID fuel-price trough (revenue 45.8bn), so the revenue CAGR measures crude prices, not the business. The 3yr figures (revenue 2.1%, FCF 10.0%) are the cleaner read.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not deducted, net borrower): FY2021 2,878.6 -> FY2023 2,512.5 -> FY2026 3,345.6. SBC is immaterial (0.03-0.04% of revenue) so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are identical to one decimal; SBC is not absorbing any of the growth. FY2021 FCF was itself flattered by COVID-year capex of 1,189 vs 1,900-2,300 since.

base.narrative: Y1 revenue +10% is fuel price (Q1 FY2027 ran +25% on price and GetGo annualisation) at an 8.5% adjusted-EBITDA margin -> adj EBITDA ~7.15bn, +6.5% on FY2026's 6.71bn, below the +10.5% Q1 run-rate to allow for fuel-margin give-back in H2. Y2-Y4 revenue +4.5% with margin creeping to 8.65% gives adj EBITDA growth ~5.7%/yr: the low end of the 6-8% Core + More guide, the gap being a haircut for FY2026-27 fuel margins (US 47-53 cpg vs a 45 cpg two-year norm). Margin lift comes from Fit-to-Serve costs and food/private-label mix, offset by nicotine decline and EV volume erosion in Europe. Lease cost 1.0% of revenue, D&A ex-ROU 2.3%, capex 2.6-2.7% (~750 new stores by 2030 plus maintenance ~2.2-2.4bn/yr), cash tax ramping 17% -> 23% as FY2025-26 bonus-depreciation deferrals unwind (cash tax 440.5 vs ~930 book in FY2026). Working capital neutral. Zabka NPV-neutral and excluded. WACC 7.5% USD, g 2.5%, cap 18x (binds: Gordon at 7.5/2.5 is 20.5x).

bull.narrative: Fuel margins hold at the structurally higher post-consolidation level (US 50+ cpg, Europe 11-12 c/l) as volumes shrink and weaker operators exit; Fit-to-Serve delivers the full $850m; food service and loyalty lift merchandise margin above 35.5%; Zabka closes on time, integrates on the TotalEnergies playbook and is accretive (carried here as ~2pp extra growth and ~0.5pp extra margin in Y2-Y5 rather than as consolidated Polish revenue). Adj EBITDA compounds ~9%/yr to FY2030, the top of guidance plus the deal. Terminal growth 3.0%, cap 20x, same 7.5% WACC.

bear.narrative: Fuel margins mean-revert in H2 FY2027 and FY2028 to the FY2023-25 band (US ~43-45 cpg, Europe ~9 c/l), taking the margin from 8.8% back to 7.6-7.7% -- the FY2023 level less a further ~0.4pp for accelerating nicotine decline (39% of merchandise), US low-income consumer stress and EV erosion of European fuel volumes (-2.2% same-store in FY2026). Zabka closes at full price into a slowing Polish consumer, lifts lease-inclusive leverage to ~2.6x, pauses buybacks and delivers no synergies in the horizon (carried as the 0% Y2 and the lower margin, not as a bridge item). Store growth continues but adds little: revenue +2%/yr, capex 2.8%, cash tax to 24%. Terminal growth 2.0%, cap 15x, same 7.5% WACC.

scenario_narratives.base: Core + More delivered at the low end: adjusted EBITDA ~5.7%/yr to FY2030 (guide 6-8%) because FY2026-27 fuel margins are a partial peak that gives some back, while Fit-to-Serve, food and private label hold the margin at 8.6-8.7%. Revenue is fuel-price noise and is modelled only to carry the margin. Zabka treated as NPV-neutral at the US$8.6bn offer. Cash tax normalises from 17% to 23% as bonus-depreciation deferrals unwind. Buybacks keep the count flat; their per-share compounding beyond that is not credited.
scenario_narratives.bull: Fuel economics stay structurally better (industry consolidation, volume-for-margin trade), Fit-to-Serve and food lift the margin above 9%, and Zabka is accretive on the TotalEnergies integration record. Adj EBITDA ~9%/yr to FY2030; management's 10%+ EPS guide is exceeded.
scenario_narratives.bear: Fuel margins revert to the FY2023-25 norm and nicotine/EV headwinds bite, taking the margin to 7.6%; Zabka adds leverage and integration cost without synergies inside the horizon; buybacks pause. EBITDA is flat for two years and grows ~2% thereafter, capitalised at 15x.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the single largest value driver -- fuel gross margin -- is at a cyclical high in the FY2026/Q1 FY2027 base (US 47-53 cpg vs 45 the two prior years) and has mean-reverted every prior cycle, and because the US$8.6bn Zabka deal is closing into that base with debt. Bull trimmed from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once: elevated fuel margins, full Fit-to-Serve delivery and an accretive cross-border integration. Base 50%: the Core + More framework is credible, the balance sheet is investment-grade (1.8x lease-inclusive pre-deal) and there is no solvency or regulatory-licence risk that would justify a heavier bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the standalone convenience/fuel platform on owner FCF with leases charged as an operating cost, fuel margins allowed to normalise, SBC expensed (immaterial), the share count held flat, and the pending Zabka acquisition held NPV-neutral at the offer price until it closes and reports. The valuation is a margin call, not a revenue call: each 0.1pp of sustained EBITDA margin is roughly US$80m of EBITDA and ~C$1.4/share.
key_risks_to_valuation: Fuel gross-margin mean reversion: FY2026 US 47.5 cpg and Q1 FY2027 52.6 cpg vs ~45 cpg in FY2024-25; every 1 cpg on ~9.7bn US gallons is ~US$97m of EBITDA

Zabka (US$8.6bn, debt-funded, Couche-Tard's largest deal) closing at full price with integration risk in a franchise model unlike its own; held NPV-neutral here, so both the accretion and the overpayment cases sit outside the base numbers
Secular nicotine decline (39% of merchandise sales) and EV erosion of European fuel volumes (-2.2% same-store FY2026) not fully offset by food service and private label
Cash-tax normalisation: FY2026 cash tax of 440.5 vs ~930 book is a timing benefit the base unwinds to 23% by Y5; a slower unwind adds value, a faster one subtracts
Terminal cap at 18x FCF binds in the base (Gordon 20.5x); the valuation is capped-multiple-sensitive rather than growth-sensitive
FX: USD flows converted to CAD at 1.4254; a 5% CAD rally is ~C$4/share with no change in the business
